0.title: Course Introduction
0.content:
Auvergne in central France is a forgotten wine paradise — an ancient landscape woven from extinct volcanoes, basalt and granite, creating some of France's most distinctive soil conditions. The Gamay and Pinot Noir of Côtes-d'Auvergne grow in 5 villages, each a "cru" with its own character; one of them — Corent — has vineyards right on the slopes of the extinct volcano Puy de Corent, and is the only cru dedicated to producing rosé!

Learning Objectives

🌋 Understand the influence of volcanic soils on wine

How basalt, granite and volcanic ash each give wine different mineral character and texture

🗺️ Grasp the differences among the five Côtes-d'Auvergne crus

From Corent's volcanic-slope rosé to Boudes' black basalt slopes, each cru has its own distinctive story

🍷 Learn how Auvergne Gamay differs from Burgundy-region Gamay

How Gamay on volcanic soils shows a personality entirely different from Beaujolais
1.title: Auvergne's Geological Revolution: What Do Volcanoes Give Wine?
1.highlights.0.title: Basalt (Basalte)
1.highlights.0.content: Cooled volcanic magma solidifies into basalt, high in iron and magnesium, giving dark black soils with very strong heat retention. Gamay planted on basalt shows deeper colour and richer black-fruit flavours, with intense minerality, similar to flint but "hotter"
1.highlights.1.title: Granite (Granite)
1.highlights.1.content: Granite is an acidic rock, containing a lot of quartz and draining well, so vine roots dig deep to find water. Pinot Noir on granite shows a leaner structure, bright acidity and delicate red-fruit character, similar to the granite personality of Morgon (Beaujolais)
1.highlights.2.title: Volcanic ash soil (Cendre Volcanique)
1.highlights.2.content: Ash left by ancient eruptions mixes with the soil to form an extremely porous structure, rich in minerals (potassium, phosphorus, sulphur), giving the wine a distinctive "smoky minerality," one of Auvergne wine's signature flavours
1.content:
Auvergne is one of France's youngest volcanic zones — the last major volcanic activity was about 8,000 years ago (the Chaîne des Puys volcanoes). Although the volcanoes are now dormant, the geological legacy they left has become a valuable asset for viticulture.

Differences between wines from volcanic and non-volcanic soils

FeatureVolcanic soil (basalt/granite)Limestone/clay
MineralityIntense smoke, saline minerals, flintFresh minerality of chalk and limestone
AcidityOften fresher acidity (affected by variety, altitude and harvest date)Softer and rounder
Pigments/phenolicsOften deeper colour and more phenolicsMore delicate (limestone style)
Typical flavoursBlack fruit, smoke, minerals, savouriness (umami)Red fruit, white flowers, cream, limestone
2.title: The Five Côtes-d'Auvergne Crus in Depth
2.content:
🌋 Corent — Rosé on an Extinct Volcano's Slope

Geology: Puy de Corent is an extinct volcano (puy), and the vineyards of the village of Corent are planted on the slopes of this ancient volcano, in soils containing volcanic materials such as basalt and volcanic scoria (pozzolana)

Varieties: mainly Gamay, the only cru of Côtes-d'Auvergne dedicated to rosé, and also one of its best-known crus

Style: Corent's rosé is extremely pale (close to onion-skin colour) and intensely mineral, with a distinctive smoky and volcanic-rock character, increasingly respected in French restaurants

What's special: tasting a Gamay rosé on the slopes of an extinct volcano is one of France's most dramatic wine experiences

🖤 Boudes — Black Basalt Slopes

Geology: deep black basalt, with dark brown-black soil and the strongest heat retention

Varieties: mainly Gamay and Pinot Noir

Style: Boudes' reds are the deepest in colour, with rich black fruit (blackberry, black plum) and abundant minerality, the most "assertive" in style of the five crus

🏰 Chateaugay — Gamay of the Castle Hill

Geology: a mix of basalt + granite, north of Clermont-Ferrand (Auvergne's capital)

Varieties: mainly Gamay

Style: lighter than Boudes, with red and black fruit side by side, the "entry-level cru" of Auvergne wine, and the most widely distributed in the market

🌹 Madargues — Home of Delicate Rosé

Geology: mainly granite

Style: granite gives higher acidity; Madargues' Gamay is known for being crisp, low in alcohol (usually 11–12%) and strongly mineral; it also makes good-quality rosé

🌿 Chanturgue — A Small Cru near Clermont-Ferrand

Location: on the slopes of the Puy de Chanturgue near Clermont-Ferrand, the smallest and rarest of the five crus

Distinction: historically known for its reds, now with tiny production and hard to find on the market

4.title: Auvergne Gamay vs Beaujolais Gamay
4.content:
Gamay has two completely different personalities in France: Beaujolais Gamay is known worldwide, but Auvergne Gamay is another world entirely.

FeatureAuvergne Gamay (volcanic soil)Beaujolais Gamay (granite/limestone)
SoilBasalt + volcanic ash (rich in iron and magnesium)Granite (Morgon/Fleurie) or limestone (Brouilly)
ColourDeeper, purple-redPaler, ruby
Main aromasBlack fruit, smoky minerality, rust (ferreux)Red fruit (strawberry/raspberry), violet, banana (if carbonic)
AcidityHigh, with a crisp feelMedium, softer and plusher
WinemakingUsually traditional (no carbonic maceration)Beaujolais Nouveau uses carbonic; fine village wines usually traditional
Market recognitionLow (Auvergne is almost nonexistent in export markets)Known worldwide (Beaujolais Nouveau culture)

Representative estate: Cave Saint-Verny (Auvergne's largest négociant, with several crus)

Travel tip: the Chaîne des Puys volcanic chain was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2018, and visiting the vineyards on the slopes of Corent is one of the highlights of Auvergne travel.
5.title: Quick Quiz
5.questions.0.question: What is the most special thing about the Côtes-d'Auvergne Corent cru?
5.questions.0.options.0: It is the largest and most productive of the five crus
5.questions.0.options.1: It is the only Côtes-d'Auvergne cru dedicated to rosé, with vineyards on the slopes of the extinct volcano Puy de Corent
5.questions.0.options.2: It is the only Auvergne cru permitted to plant Chenin Blanc
5.questions.0.options.3: Its wine must be aged on the seabed (underwater cellar)
5.questions.0.explanation: Corent is the only one of Côtes-d'Auvergne's five crus dedicated to rosé, with vineyards on the slopes of the extinct volcano Puy de Corent. The volcanic soil gives Corent rosé intense minerality and smokiness.
5.questions.1.question: What is the main reason for the stylistic difference between Auvergne Gamay and Beaujolais Gamay?
5.questions.1.options.0: They are different Gamay clones, genetically distinct
5.questions.1.options.1: Auvergne's basalt and volcanic-ash soils (rich in iron and magnesium) give deeper colour and smoky minerality, entirely different from Beaujolais' granite/limestone style
5.questions.1.options.2: Auvergne has markedly higher annual rainfall, leaving the grapes with less sugar
5.questions.1.options.3: Beaujolais only permits organic farming, and Auvergne has no such restriction
5.questions.1.explanation: Even with the same Gamay variety, soil differences create entirely different personalities: Auvergne's basalt and volcanic ash are rich in iron and magnesium minerals, giving Gamay deeper colour, black fruit, smoky minerality and a rust-like note; Beaujolais' granite brings out lighter red-fruit and violet character.
